12.t: Working with data: stopping on different roads
q: On which surface is the braking distance longest?
How much further does the car travel on a wet road than a dry road?
Use the data to explain why worn tyres are dangerous on wet roads.
With worn tyres the braking distance is 30 m compared with 20 m: less tread, less grip (friction), so the car slides further before stopping.
A school wants a sign for drivers in the rainy season. Use the data to suggest what it should say and why.

"Slow down and leave a bigger gap when wet": braking distance rises by about half on wet roads and more than doubles with worn tyres; lower speed and good tyres keep friction high and stopping distance short.
